issues.summary: Binding only filters attested events. Proposals from another chain or Safe for the same safeTxHash, plus the requestIds, sentinel logs and ORACLE_RESULT events derived from them, still reach deriveCheckState. A foreign rejection can therefore show MALICIOUS (or TIMED_OUT) for the Safe being viewed and get pinned. The existing test locks this in.
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: attestations.ts:44-46 keeps any non-attested event (`!isAttested(event) || ...`), even though proposal events carry chainId/safe (types/events.ts:42-43,71-72). safenetReader.ts:318-337 builds requestIds from every allowlisted proposal. deriveCheckState.ts:71 then returns MALICIOUS on any negative ORACLE_RESULT, and safenetCheckApi.ts:99-100 pins it. The chain-B test (safenetCheckApi.test.ts:495-505) expects SUBMITTED from a proposal bound to chain A. The attacker-driven variant in F16 depends on on-chain validation that can't be checked here, but the cross-chain leak itself is real.

issues.summary: The BENIGN arbitration window returns 0 when the client clock is slightly behind the attested block's timestamp (negative age). A check is usually first seen as BENIGN seconds after it is attested, so a few seconds of skew turns off the new arbitration poll for that mount.
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: computePollingInterval.ts:66-68 returns 0 whenever age < 0. With interval 0 no fetch lands, so fulfilledAt never changes and the effect in useSafenetCheck.ts:97-126 never re-runs. The zero is never re-evaluated, so the feature is quietly lost for fresh checks. The tests at computePollingInterval.test.ts:57-64 assert this stop behaviour.

issues.summary: Once the interval is 0, polling never restarts during the mount.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: This is the intended, documented ceiling: computePollingInterval.ts:63-64 says an arbitration landing after the window is 'only picked up by a page reload'. Past the window, stopping is the design. The skew-triggered early stop is covered separately under F11.

issues.summary: A failed blockTimeMs read gives a null attestedAtMs and stops BENIGN polling.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: This is deliberate and documented. The PR's Risks section says a failed header read closes the arbitration window for that session, and safenetReader.ts:465-467 returns null on purpose so a missing date never suppresses a verdict.

issues.summary: verdictAttestation, which picks the audit row's proof link, has no test covering several candidates, null signatureId, or the logIndex tie-break.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: Its only consumer is SafenetAuditRow.tsx:67, and the SafenetAuditRow tests (lines 68-143) use a single attested event. So choosing the proof link among several attestations, which this PR changed, goes untested.

issues.summary: No test covers an INVALID oracle attestation followed by a VERIFIED plain one.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The selection tests (safenetCheckApi.test.ts:357-428) cover newest vs earliest within a family and the oracle-first order, but not this mixed-family fall-through. With oracle events present, deriveCheckState.ts:75-78 would return BENIGN on the plain event's VERIFIED result, and nothing pins that down.

issues.summary: The familyRank comment implies plain attestations aren't verified while oracle ones exist, but selectAttestation falls through to them.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: attestations.ts:7-9 says verifying a plain event while an oracle one exists 'would answer a question the status machine never asks'. But safenetCheckApi.ts:48-54 keeps verifying later candidates, including plain ones, after an oracle event fails.

issues.summary: attestationCandidates has no dedicated unit test file.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: It isn't exported, and its ordering is exercised through the selection tests in safenetCheckApi.test.ts:357-428 (newest-first, oracle-first). A separate file would add little.

issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The cases F8 lists as untested (other chain, other Safe, mixed-case address) are tested at safenetCheckApi.test.ts:447-493, just through the query rather than directly.

issues.summary: bindAttestations lowercases the address by hand instead of calling sameAddress.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: attestations.ts:43-45 compares lowercased strings. sameAddress (packages/utils/src/utils/addresses.ts:24) does the same thing plus empty-string handling, and the hook already gates out an empty safeAddress (useSafenetCheck.ts:50). This is a consistency point with no concrete cost.

issues.summary: TxSigners passes safe.address.value while the other callers pass useSafeInfo's safeAddress.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: TxSigners/index.tsx:173 uses safe.address.value, which is exactly the value useSafeInfo exposes as safeAddress. The values are the same, so this is purely stylistic.

issues.summary: The oracle and plain attested branches in deriveCheckState are identical and could be merged.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: deriveCheckState.ts:75-89 repeats the same three-way return. Merging them would keep the behaviour unchanged, so this is purely a readability preference.

issues.summary: The checklist was written to the scratchpad instead of docs/engineering/.
issues.label: unverifiable
issues.evidence: This is about where a generated artifact was saved, not about the PR's code, and the diff gives no way to settle it.
